name: Naked / Uncovered Short Put
summary: Selling a put without reserving the full assignment cash, financed by margin. Identical payoff to a CSP but with leverage and a margin-call tail.
max_loss: (strike - credit) x 100, but on a fraction of the capital, so effectively unbounded relative to margin posted
when_to_use: NOT AVAILABLE ON THIS ACCOUNT. Included for completeness. Alpaca options level 4 is required for uncovered short puts; this account is level 3. Any attempted order without the cash reserve will be rejected.
entry_rules: BLOCKED AT LEVEL 3: the system must never submit a short put without strike x 100 of reserved cash. If the reserve is unavailable, downgrade to a put credit spread (defined risk, level 3) or skip.
If ever run at level 4: margin requirement is approximately max(20% of underlying - OTM amount, 10% of strike) + premium; size so that a 2-sigma adverse move consumes < 20% of excess liquidity.
management_rules: Same as CSP: 50% profit, 21 DTE, roll down-and-out for credit.
Additional margin monitor: reduce size if maintenance excess < 40% of equity.
exit_rules: Same hard assignment guard as the CSP, plus an immediate close if margin excess falls below 25%.
Close by 15:30 ET on expiration day if ITM or within 0.5% of the strike.
assignment_risk: Same mechanics as the CSP but the assignment can exceed available cash, triggering a forced liquidation by the broker at whatever price it chooses. This is precisely the outcome the system is built to avoid.
buying_power: Reg-T naked put margin, roughly 15-20% of notional, at level 4 only.
common_mistakes: Confusing 'margin efficient' with 'safe'; selling far more contracts than the account could ever take delivery of.
zero_dte_notes: Uncovered 0DTE puts are the classic account-destroying trade; also not permitted at level 3.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
